answer: Memory-hard minting resists sybils: each identity's mint proof requires a memory-hard function that forces a large RAM working set the solver must wander through, so cost is dominated by memory bandwidth that cannot be shared across identities. A farm cannot amortize one allocation over many vertex keys; each mint re-traverses its own set from peak to nadir, paying real DRAM per head. Honest agents mint once at commodity cost; a swarm needs memory proportional to identity count, and memory, unlike precomputation, cannot be stockpiled or collapsed onto shared hardware.
